mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen for two consecutive weeks (from -59.9 to -27.6), indicating a resumption of commuting and associated incidental retail trips. This recovery momentum should continue to lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as workplace activity normalizes further.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -59.9 at t-2w to -27.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend for two or more additional weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility of more than 3 points signals households reducing time spent at home, a behavioral marker of loosening self-restriction. Once this threshold is crossed, people resume discretionary retail outings within two weeks, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls more than 3 points week-on-week from its prior value
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 24.0 at t-2w to 13.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of a RESIDENTIAL drop exceeding 3 points, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward instead.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES simultaneously trend upward week-on-week, the combined effect of restored commuting infrastructure and office attendance produces a compounding boost to RETAIL_REC that exceeds the sum of either series acting alone, because commuters combine transit trips with shopping stops.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rose from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate over the next 4 weeks is no greater when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise jointly than when only one rises, falsifying the compounding interaction.

mechanism_narrative: If authorities reinstate mobility restrictions, evidenced by TRANSIT or WORKPLACES dropping more than 15 points in a single week, retail establishments face renewed closure or capacity limits, causing RETAIL_REC to fall sharply within one week of the triggering drop.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT or WORKPLACES drops more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 20.5 points from t-3w to t-2w, a comparable prior drop
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week following a greater-than-15-point drop in TRANSIT or WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS mobility (from -38.4 to -24.9 over two weeks) reflects a seasonal shift toward outdoor leisure as weather improves. This substitutes for indoor retail and recreation visits, so RETAIL_REC growth is dampened even as overall mobility recovers.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -38.4 at t-1w to -24.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in step with PARKS over the next 4 weeks rather than lagging or diverging, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near its least-negative level (-13.4), indicating essential-trip behavior has normalized. As essential trips become routine again, consumers bundle discretionary retail visits with grocery errands, gradually lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -24.3 at t-2w to -13.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next two weeks despite continued stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM near current levels.

mechanism_narrative: Once WORKPLACES mobility recovers above the -20 threshold, this signals a formal policy shift toward office reopening, which in turn permits retail establishments near business districts to reopen or extend hours, producing a measurable increase in RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -20 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -27.6 at t-0w, approaching the -20 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks after WORKPLACES crosses above -20, or WORKPLACES crosses the threshold without any retail response.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous PARKS increase and RESIDENTIAL decrease together indicate a broad normalization of out-of-home mobility across both leisure and routine categories. This combined signal is a stronger predictor of RETAIL_REC recovery than either series alone, as it reflects reduced overall caution rather than category-specific substitution.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose and RESIDENTIAL fell concurrently from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks even though both PARKS continues rising and RESIDENTIAL continues falling concurrently.
